- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.17 or +0.23) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.11 or -0.22) — model fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often overreacts to sentiment shifts 1–2 days later, so adjust forecasts by reducing 1–2 days’ peak values if sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows; apply smoothing or decay to recent values when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term sentiment momentum — reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model tends to ignore the trend — apply downward bias to forecast if sentiment is positive but price action contradicts it.
